""""
Task
----
The user needs a corrected VBA macro that deletes the FOUR rows located
immediately ABOVE (before) every occurrence of the text "Chassis" in
column A of the sheet named "Import Data".  In the user's workbook the two
"Chassis" entries sit in A2 and A3, so the corrected macro must also cope
with the case where fewer than four rows exist above a "Chassis" cell
(i.e. it must never reference/delete rows above row 1 - the bug that makes
the original top-down code crash).  The fix is to loop from the BOTTOM of
the data upwards and clamp the start of the deleted range to row 1.

Deliverable
-----------
The corrected 15-line VBA macro is written (one line per cell) into
Sheet1!A1:A15 of output.xlsx, which is created as a copy of the provided
input workbook.
"""

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import Workbook, load_workbook

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0.  Paths
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
WORKDIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent if "__file__" in globals() else Path(".")
OUTPUT_PATH = WORKDIR / "output.xlsx"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Locate the provided input workbook and copy it to output.xlsx
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def find_input_workbook():
    for name in ("input.xlsx", "input.xlsm", "input.xls",
                 "Import Data.xlsx", "data.xlsx", "workbook.xlsx"):
        candidate = WORKDIR / name
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    # fall back to any Excel file in the folder except the output file
    others = sorted(p for p in WORKDIR.glob("*.xls*")
                    if p.name.lower() != "output.xlsx")
    return others[0] if others else None


input_path = find_input_workbook()

if input_path is not None:
    shutil.copy(input_path, OUTPUT_PATH)          # output = copy of the input book
    print(f"Copied '{input_path.name}' -> '{OUTPUT_PATH.name}'")
else:
    # No workbook supplied -> build a small stand-in so the script still runs
    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Import Data"
    ws["A1"] = "Header row"
    ws["A2"] = "Chassis"                          # the two "Chassis" cells (A2 & A3)
    ws["A3"] = "Chassis"
    for row, value in enumerate(("Data 1", "Data 2", "Data 3"), start=4):
        ws.cell(row=row, column=1, value=value)
    wb.create_sheet("Sheet1")
    wb.save(OUTPUT_PATH)
    print(f"No input workbook found - created stand-in '{OUTPUT_PATH.name}'")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.  The corrected VBA macro  (exactly 15 lines -> Sheet1!A1:A15)
#     * loops bottom-up so deletions cannot shift unprocessed rows
#     * clamps the delete start to row 1 (Chassis in A2/A3 would otherwise
#       produce negative row references -> runtime error)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VBA_CODE = "\n".join([
    'Sub DeleteRowsBeforeChassis()',
    '    Dim ws As Worksheet, i As Long, r As Long',
    '    Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Import Data")',
    '    i = ws.Cells(ws.Rows.Count, "A").End(xlUp).Row',
    '    Do While i >= 2',
    '        If Trim(CStr(ws.Cells(i, "A").Value)) = "Chassis" Then',
    '            r = i - 4',
    '            If r < 1 Then r = 1',
    '            ws.Rows(r & ":" & (i - 1)).Delete',
    '            i = r - 1',
    '        Else',
    '            i = i - 1',
    '        End If',
    '    Loop',
    'End Sub',
])

lines = VBA_CODE.splitlines()
assert len(lines) == 15, f"Expected 15 VBA lines, got {len(lines)}"
